newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean yields end higher on Kia bail-out news.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean yields end higher on Kia bail-out news.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates ended higher on Tuesday as fears of the impact from financial troubles at the Kia Group dampened buying sentiment, brokers said.
The Korea First Bank, Kia's main creditor, said 18 of the group's 38 affiliates would be bailed out.
Three-month CDs and the overnight call rate also edged up in slow trading, they said.
* 3-yr corporates end at 11.95 pct vs 11.87 pct on Monday
* 3-mth CDs close at 11.90 pct vs 11.75 pct
* Overnight call average 11.50 pct from 11.40 pct
New issues of three-year corporates were estimated at 175 billion won on Wednesday, against 68 billion won today.
Brokers said the three-year yields, South Korea's benchmark interest rates, would hover around 12.00 percent for the time being.
Three-month CDs and the overnight call rate also rose in weak trading, reflecting worries over tightening liquidity, they said.
